documents.text: Are eggs bad for your heart? For most healthy people, eating up to seven eggs a week does not raise the risk of heart disease. If you have high cholesterol you may need to watch how many you eat.
How many eggs can you eat on a heart-healthy diet? One large egg has about 186 mg of cholesterol, all in the yolk, but eggs are also rich in choline and vitamins.
Should I stop eating eggs? The foods people eat with eggs, like bacon and sausage, may do more to raise heart-disease risk than eggs themselves.
Saturated fat and cardiovascular disease: the importance of inter-individual variation in the response of serum low-density lipoprotein cholesterol.
Individual variation in plasma cholesterol response to dietary saturated fat. Some people show a much larger rise in blood cholesterol than others after the same intake.

Hyper- and hypo-responsiveness in serum LDL cholesterol to dietary cholesterol reflects a variable capacity to absorb cholesterol in the gut; consistent hyper-responders show large mean differences between high- and low-fat diets.
The benefits of measuring the size and number of lipoprotein particles for cardiovascular risk prediction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Clinical relevance of nuclear magnetic resonance lipoprotein particle profiling; particle number can be discordant with cholesterol concentration.
Patients with a discordant high number of low-density lipoprotein particles despite low cholesterol levels carry underestimated cardiovascular risk.
Food substitution models for nutritional epidemiology: the leave-one-out model and the energy partition model estimate relative causal effects.
Identification and estimation of average causal effects under dietary substitution strategies, holding total energy fixed.
Adjustment for energy intake in nutritional research: a causal-inference perspective on substitution effects and residual confounding.
A hierarchical Bayesian model for forecasting quarterly retail sales under promotional interventions.
Comparative performance of transformer architectures on long-context document retrieval benchmarks.
